meta.description: Watches any number of sender domains and only wakes an agent when mail actually arrives. The scan runs through Mark VI's own Gmail connection — no second credential, no model, no tokens. Everything is configured in ONE node: 'Mail list'. Fork per agent if you want different voices answering. Safe to activate with an empty list.

nodes.name: Every 10 minutes
nodes.notes:
Mail arrives at any hour, so this runs around the clock — 144 scans a day, each one HTTP request and zero tokens.

Every rule in the list is checked on this one schedule. Widening it to */30 only delays a push; the SPEDA-Seen label means a longer gap can never lose a message.

nodes.name: Mail list
nodes.notes:
⚙️ EDIT HERE — the whole configuration surface. One block per domain, in the MAILS array. The comment block documents every field.

Each entry becomes one item and every node downstream runs once per item, so watching five senders needs no other change.

TO FORK: duplicate the workflow, keep only the rules you want in it, rename it, activate. Rules in different workflows are independent.

nodes.name: Igor: scan mail
nodes.notes:
THE CHEAP HALF — runs once per rule, taking all its settings from the list. Nothing to edit here.

Igor queries `from:<domain> -label:<label> newer_than:2d` against the owner's Gmail using the connection from Settings ▸ Google Workspace, then re-checks each hit's From header strictly. No LLM, so a quiet mailbox costs nothing.

neverError: one failing rule must not fail the run and take the others with it. The gate inspects each response.

nodes.name: Gate
nodes.notes:
The cost boundary — everything downstream spends money, everything upstream does not. On a normal run every rule reports zero and this returns no items, which stops the branch.

pairedItem is set explicitly so the mark-seen node can find its own rule's message ids.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ ({ "payload": { "type": "watchdog", "event": "new_mail", "job": "mail_watch", "automation": "Mail watch — " + $json.domain, "source": "gmail", "domain": $json.domain, "count": $json.count, "messages": $json.messages, "intent": $json.alert ? ("Your mail watch for " + $json.domain + " cannot read Gmail right now (" + $json.detail + "). Tell the owner in one short line that the watch is blind and Google likely needs reconnecting in Settings. Do not call any tool.") : $json.intent }, "output_mode": "push" }) }}

nodes.name: Igor: trigger agent
nodes.notes:
THE EXPENSIVE HALF — one agentic turn per rule that found mail. The agent comes from the rule, so the URL is an expression; nothing to edit here.

No neverError, deliberately: a failure must kill the branch BEFORE mark-seen, leaving the mail unlabelled so the next poll retries it. Retries cover the 503 the trigger endpoint returns when the turn registry is at capacity.

nodes.name: Igor: mark seen
nodes.notes:
Labels exactly the messages just handed to the agent, so the next scan skips them. This is what stops the same mail pushing every 10 minutes. Unread state is untouched — the mail still looks new in the inbox.

$('Gate').item — not .first() — so when two rules both find mail, each ack labels ITS OWN messages.

Deliberately AFTER the trigger: labelling first would lose a message whenever the notify call failed. On the blind-watch alert path message_ids is empty and this is a no-op.
